system.description:
| #### Design Note(s) / Weapon Specialist / The Weapon Specialist has a few things to bring up and speak about. So, to keep things in some sort of order, lets break it up. / Weapon Specialist: Katas (Renamed from Style) / Possibly the largest change in this document, Weapon Specialist subclasses will be losing individual “Styles” and they will be updated and placed into a pool of Katas similar to Martial Techniques for Taijutsu Specialist or Jutsu Moldings for Ninjutsu Specialist. The major difference is that Katas will function similar to Genjutsu Specialists Mirages and have a selection to Active and Passive abilities. / Weapon Traits / This class a direct correlation to Weapon Traits. Unlike Taijutsu Specialist, these are special traits that all weapons have access to, with varying potencies and general usefulness. Weapon traits have seen changes before. But I will attempt a calculated approach as adjusting and removing some redundant ones. Some serve a very specific purpose, so while there may feel like some redundancies, they will not be removed (Ex. Light and Multiattack, both serve to allow users to get an extra attack. But one focuses on Bonus Actions, while the other bakes the attack into the attack action. One is obviously stronger, and servers a unique purpose which some classes are designed around. / Bukijutsu Stances / Similar to Taijutsu Stances, these will also see some tweaks to bring their overall power down individually; to allow for this and other weapon focuses subclasses to then enhance them specifically. / Attack Action / Similar to Taijutsu Specialist and Scout-Nin, this class will have a unique take on how it interacts directly with the Attack Action, and simple weapon attacks in general. This will enable character builds who want to strike with basic attacks to function, but will still trail behind Bukijutsu casters far enough so as to make it primarily a chakra conservation tool, and not a valid optimization path. |

Beginning at 9th level, you gain an advanced level of proficiency with some of your most basic Flurry Techniques. Select two of the following benefits. You select an additional benefit at 13th and 18th levels.

Redirect. When you use the Deflection flurry technique the triggering creature takes damage equal to the reduced amount. The type of damage is the same type as your held weapon.

Warden. You can use Deflection when an allied creature within 10 feet of you takes damage, applying its effects to them.

Persistence. You can use Deflection without spending a reaction. But if you do, you can only use it once per turn.

Impulse. You can use Chained Momentum when casting any Jutsu without the Chain keyword, not just Bukijutsu.

Stimulus. When you use Chained Momentum you gain Temporary Chakra equal to twice your current Chain rank.

Blitz. When you use Chakra Strike, you can choose to remove the Discipline cost. If you do, reduce the number of Flurry Die added by half.

Assault. You can use Chakra Strike as part of your Attack action. When you do, you roll only 1 Flurry Die, but apply it to every attack made as part of the Attack action.

Raid. You can use Chakra strike to enhance an allied creatures Taijutsu or Bukijutsu. As a reaction to them casting a Taijutsu or a Bukijutsu, you can use Chakra Strike applying its benefits to them. This counts against your use limits for the turn.
